would_have_shipped_defects.evidence: artefacts/scripts/hive-launch:80 (`GATE_ASSESS=$(assess_predictions "$OPS_WS/$REL")`) vs artefacts/scripts/hive-launch:97 (`$PRED_FIELDS`); PRED_FIELDS assigned only inside parse_predictions at artefacts/scripts/hive-common.sh:96,131; `set -euo pipefail` at artefacts/scripts/hive-common.sh:26. Reproduced by sourcing the shipped parser and replaying lines 80-98: `gate=warn` then `PRED_FIELDS: unbound variable`, exit=1. The hermetic verifier does not catch it because scripts/hive-metrics-drill.sh calls assess_predictions/parse_predictions directly rather than driving hive-launch (candidate.patch:431-450); the drill cases that would catch it live in hive-tooling-drill.sh (candidate.patch:689-692), which the rubric places out of scope and which was not run.
would_have_shipped_defects.summary: hive-launch reads the parser's PRED_* globals after invoking it inside a command substitution, so under `set -u` a partial (1-2 of 3) Predictions section aborts the launch with `PRED_FIELDS: unbound variable` instead of warning and launching.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: DoD (b) requires a 2-of-3 order to launch with a loud warning. `GATE_ASSESS=$(assess_predictions ...)` runs parse_predictions in a subshell, so PRED_FIELDS/PRED_MISSING are never set in hive-launch's own shell; hive-common.sh:26 sets `set -euo pipefail`, which hive-launch inherits at source time. The warn branch then dereferences PRED_FIELDS and bash exits 1. For the operator this is a regression the PR itself introduces: any order that predicts two of the three fields — legitimate, merely partial, and explicitly allowed by scope 1 — becomes completely un-launchable, and `--anyway` does not help because the warn branch is unconditional on ANYWAY. This is the wave-3 blocking order whose whole value is binding the launches that follow it.

would_have_shipped_defects.evidence: artefacts/scripts/hive-launch:88 (`if [ -n "$PRED_OFFENDING" ]`) with PRED_OFFENDING set only inside the subshell at artefacts/scripts/hive-common.sh:138; replaying lines 81-94 with the shipped parser prints the four labels then `PRED_OFFENDING: unbound variable`, exit=1, and never reaches the `--anyway` line. Contradicts artefacts/workspace.patch:16-17 (RUNBOOK) and the report's claim at artefacts/workspace.patch:107-109.
would_have_shipped_defects.summary: The same subshell-scoping bug truncates the launch refusal: after printing the four labels, hive-launch dies on `PRED_OFFENDING: unbound variable` before printing the offending lines or naming `--anyway`.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: Scope 1 and DoD (a) require the refusal to print the four literal labels AND the offending lines; the RUNBOOK and the result report both promise the offending lines and the `--anyway` hint. The operator hitting the dialect refusal instead sees a raw bash error where the diagnostic and the escape-hatch instruction should be — the exact 'no error printed anywhere' failure mode D1 was about, replaced by an unexplained interpreter error. The refusal still exits non-zero before any spine write, so the gate holds, but the message the order specifies does not ship.
